newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa higher but off new one-year peak.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa higher but off new one-year peak.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures extended Thursday's advance on follow-through buying and prices ended Friday midsession higher but off their new one-year peak basis September.
September broke the immediate 1,140 stg a tonne barrier to hit the session high of 1,141 but stepped back a bit to battle with the 1,130 mark. It finished the morning trade five stg up at 1,135.
"The 1,130 level is being defended at the moment," said one. "Chart-wise, a close above 1,130 marks a key day reserval."
The gains followed carry-over buying from Thursday but the volume was markedly lower. Turnover reached just 2,330 lots by midday.
New York's strength on Thursday also lent some support in London this morning, encouraging further buying by locals, specs and a few trade houses.
Cocoa's rally since last week was mainly chart-driven but some traders said bulls were also encouraged by a promising longer-term fundamental picture
Cocoa pod counters are not due to return from West Africa until the beginning of July but very preliminary forecasts point to a less favourable supply prospects in Ivory Coast.
But others said with the current "silly season" in cocoa, they could expect a lot of crop rumours.

Early 1997/98 Ivory Coast crop estimates vary from a 785,000 tonnes-mark (main crop) by U.S.-based crop analyst Hans Kilian, according to traders, to a more optimistic 1.1 million tonnes for the whole of 1997/98 by Swiss chocolate giant Callebaut Barry, which has two factories in Ivory Coast.

In other news, British trader ED&F Man Group Plc said on Friday it signed a definitive deal to sell its cocoa processing business to U.S. group Archer Daniels Midland Co for $108 million in cash plus the assumption of debt.
ED&F said ADM would discharge intra-group debt of $35 million and assume third-party bank indebtedness of $80 million.
It said it would retain its profitable cocoa sourcing operations and its international cocoa merchanting business.
